title: Classroom Activities · The Wonderful World of Science
chapter_focus: Building observation, questioning, and basic experimental thinking.

activities.title: Mystery Bag
activities.objective: Practise observation by identifying objects from non-visual clues.
materials: 5 small everyday items per bag (e.g. coin, eraser, comb, key, button)
Notebook and pencil for each group

steps.title: Set up
steps.detail: Make sure each cloth bag has the same 5 items but in random order. Don't show the items to the students.

steps.title: Round 1: feel only
steps.detail: Each student in turn reaches in WITHOUT LOOKING and writes down what they think is inside the bag. They list shape, size, weight, texture.

steps.title: Group share
steps.detail: After everyone has had a turn, the group compares notes and writes a single agreed-on list.

steps.title: Reveal and reflect
steps.detail: Open the bag together. Compare predictions with reality. Discuss what features helped and which guesses were wrong.

guiding_questions: What features were easiest to notice without seeing?
Which items were guessed correctly by everyone? Why?
Which were tricky? What detail would have helped?
How is this similar to what scientists do?
safety_notes: Do not put sharp objects in the bag.
variations: For older classes, include items from chemistry/biology kits.
For struggling pairs, allow listening (shake the bag) as an extra clue.

activities.title: Question Storm
activities.objective: Generate testable scientific questions about an everyday phenomenon.
materials: A simple object: a candle, a flowerpot, or a glass of water
A wall or board to post the notes

steps.title: Show
steps.detail: Place the object on a desk where everyone can see it.

steps.title: Storm
steps.detail: Each student writes ONE question per sticky note (max 5 questions). Encourage 'why', 'how', 'what if'. No question is too small.

steps.title: Cluster
steps.detail: Together, group similar questions on the wall.

steps.title: Pick a winner
steps.detail: Vote on the BEST scientific question — one that's specific and testable.

guiding_questions: Which questions can we answer by careful observation?
Which are not really scientific (e.g. 'is it pretty?')?
How would we test the chosen winner question?
variations: Use a Diwali diya for cultural connect.
For younger groups, give a starter question stem like 'What happens when…'.
